The US Edition of SNOMED CT combines the International Release of SNOMED CT and the US Extension of SNOMED CT

SNOMED CT provides the core general terminology for the electronic health record (EHR). The concepts have unique meanings and formal logic-based definitions organized into hierarchies. Each International Release includes the core of the terminology (concepts, descriptions, and relationships), together with works to support the implementation and use of SNOMED CT, including subsets, cross maps to existing classifications and coding schemes, and an extensive set of guidelines.

The US Extension to SNOMED CT included the concepts, descriptions, and relationships accepted by NLM as a formal extension to the SNOMED CT International Release. NLM no longer releases the standalone US Extension.

The US Edition of SNOMED CT includes more than 300,000 unique concepts. There are over 1,000,000 descriptions in SNOMED CT, including synonyms that can be used to refer to a concept. In addition, there are approximately 903,000 links or semantic relationships between the SNOMED CT concepts.

seed_rows.title: Natural Kinds, Psychiatric Classification and the History of the DSM

seed_rows.title: The Nature of Disease

seed_rows.title: Tendencies and Other Realizables in Medical Information Sciences

seed_rows.title: Concepts and Causes in the Philosophy of Disease

seed_rows.title: Do We Need a Concept of Disease?

seed_rows.title: Fuzzy Health, Illness, and Disease

seed_rows.relevance: Argues disease is an inherently graded/fuzzy concept — directly relevant to crisp-class vs. vague-boundary modelling decisions.

seed_rows.title: Defining Disease: Much Ado about Nothing?
seed_rows.relevance: Deflationary take questioning the value of the definitional project; useful counterweight when justifying your own definition.

seed_rows.title: The Concepts of Health and Disease

seed_rows.title: What Is It to Be Healthy?

seed_rows.title: Philosophy of Medicine
seed_rows.relevance: Recent monograph with sustained chapters on defining disease and on causation/explanation in medicine; good orientation text.

seed_rows.title: Concepts of Disease and Health
seed_rows.relevance: The standard survey of the whole debate (naturalism, normativism, hybrids). No DOI but the canonical entry point/reference.

seed_rows.title: On the Nature of Health: An Action-Theoretic Approach (2nd ed.)
seed_rows.relevance: The major holistic / action-theoretic alternative to both Boorse and the disposition view; defines health via ability to reach vital goals.
